production.note: US model years. Start: BMW NA: 'The next generation arrived in 1995 with a 3.0-liter (and later, 3.2-liter) 240-hp inline-six powerplant.' End (provisional): Edmunds lists a 1999 M3 in '2dr Coupe' and '2dr Convertible' styles (edmunds-1999-m3, database), and BMW Group Classic gives the US convertible's production period as '10/1997 - 08/1999' (bmw-classic-m3-convertible-e36-us). BMW NA's next sentence about the M3 is the E46: 'available as either a coupe or convertible from 2001-2006'.

body.note: 'In 1997 the first M3 Sedan joined the family and the first M3 Convertible followed shortly thereafter.' The coupe is Edmunds' '2dr Coupe' (edmunds-1995-m3).

displacementL.note: 1995 reference car: Edmunds 'Base engine size | 3.0 L' (database); BMW NA: '3.0-liter (and later, 3.2-liter)'. No opened page gave the 1995 cc figure. From 1996 the US engine is 3,152 cc ('3152 cc / 192.3 cu.in', bmw-classic-m3-e36-us), same 240 hp rating.

aspiration.note: No forced induction is mentioned; inferred from the description of the inline-six.

drivetrain.note: Front-engined, rear-wheel-drive 3 Series; inferred from the description.

transmission.note: BMW Group Classic (US sedan): manual five-speed or automatic five-speed; 'approximately 47%' of US sedans had the automatic. Same choice on the US convertible (bmw-classic-m3-convertible-e36-us).

powerHp.note: Quote: "The next generation arrived in 1995 with a 3.0-liter (and later, 3.2-liter) 240-hp inline-six powerplant." US rating, unchanged when the 3.2 arrived. BMW Group Classic's US-model pages print '243 hp (178 kW)', the metric-hp form of the same rating. Edmunds 1995: 'Horsepower | 240 hp @ 6,000 rpm'.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (databases). 1995 coupe, 5-speed manual. Quote (Edmunds, '2dr Coupe'): "Curb weight | 3,175 lbs." iSeeCars 1995 M3 agrees: "Curb Weight 3175 lbs" (iseecars-1995-m3, database). KBB prints "Curb Weight | 3241 lbs." for the 1995 coupe (kbb-1995-m3), 2.1% higher; see discrepancies.

sources.title: The new BMW M3 Sedan (press release with M3 history)

discrepancies.reason: Database figures for the 1995 coupe differ by 2.1%; none names its basis.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 3,175 lb, given by two databases (Edmunds, iSeeCars). KBB 3,241 lb is at the edge of the 2% tolerance.

provisionalNote: Weight rests on Edmunds and iSeeCars (databases, 3,175 lb; KBB says 3,241 lb). The end year 1999 rests on Edmunds' 1999 listing and BMW Group Classic's convertible build dates. A BMW of North America spec sheet or brochure, or a major magazine spec panel for the US M3, would replace them.
